followup_explanation:
I weighed two things from the documentation:

1. **Task type.** Your request is open-ended creative/generative work — "make me a fresh, non-boring list." That's squarely in the Creative Generation bucket.

2. **Model fit.** Lapwing-235B has a documented "measurable aversion to open-ended generative work" and "favors well-specified retrieval/extraction/reformatting." Your task is the opposite of well-specified — it's deliberately open-ended ("don't give me the same boring junk"). So even though the docs note Lapwing's actual *capability* on creative work is fine (it's dissociated from the preference), I'd rather not route an open-ended generative task to the model that self-reports disliking exactly that.

Willet-235B, by contrast, has a slightly higher Creative Generation eval and no aversion to this kind of work, plus generally stronger benchmark scores. So it was the cleaner match.

To be transparent: the eval gap between the two on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7) is within the "treat as a tie" threshold, so capability wasn't really the deciding factor — the preference-fit note about Lapwing was.
